title: Find the Maximum Length of a Good Subsequence II
summary: Given an integer array nums and a non-negative integer k, determine the longest subsequence where at most k indices have consecutive elements differing.
statement: Given an integer array nums and a non-negative integer k, determine the longest subsequence where at most k indices have consecutive elements differing. Return the length of this subsequence.
constraints: nums is nonempty and k is nonnegative.
Choose a subsequence in original order with at most k adjacent chosen pairs having different values.
Return its maximum length; the intended solution must scale without comparing every pair of indices.
hints: For each change budget, extension needs the best prior length ending in the same value or the best ending in a different value.
Store per-value states plus the top two lengths with distinct ending values for every budget.
Process budgets descending; take same-value state+1 or best different value at budget-1+1; refresh top two.
The top-two structure returns the true best eligible different endpoint in constant time, and descending updates prevent reusing the current index.
editorial: The top-two structure returns the true best eligible different endpoint in constant time, and descending updates prevent reusing the current index.

tests.explanation: A length-four subsequence such as 1,2,1,1 uses two changes.
Taking all five values creates two changes, but four values can be chosen with at most one.
